correctness.rationale: An independent exhaustive construction started from all 720 permutations and took two successive one-symbol deletions, re-ranking after each by subtracting one from each remaining label greater than the deleted label. This retains only relative order; composing it twice gives precisely the 15 retained-position possibilities with duplicates discarded. Grouping by literal frozensets, not by the source's bitmask or rank sorting, returned 710 singleton fibers and exactly the listed tripletons {132465,132546,213546} and {564231,645231,645312}, and doubletons {241635,315264} and {462513,536142}, with deck sizes five and ten respectively. Reversal and complement swap the two fibers of each size; inversion fixes each fiber setwise. These operations commute with taking subpatterns when applied also to the patterns, and none of the exceptional sources has fewer than two descents. The 58 sources with at most one descent can also be counted as 1+(2^6−7): choose the first increasing run as a nonempty proper subset and exclude the five initial intervals (the splits of the increasing word). A full-deck decoder admits one representative per fiber, hence 714 as the maximum size and 3×2×2×3=36 distinct labeled maximum codebooks.
residual_risks: The census is exhaustive at n=6 only. Deck injectivity does not imply unique decoding from a single arbitrary standardized deletion trace.

value.rationale: Six is the last ambiguous length for this natural observation; it is not an arbitrary small cutoff. Resolving every exceptional labeled source at that threshold quantifies exactly what information the full set loses, gives an optimal decoding dictionary and all its degrees of freedom, and identifies symmetry and descent restrictions on ambiguity. These are useful in reconstruction questions that assume complete access to distinct patterns, not merely as a repeat of a known threshold.
residual_risks: The gain is a finite reconstruction classification, not a guarantee for ordinary single-trace deletion codes or a new asymptotic bound.
